A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TSR method and applications. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–C are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy-distribution experiments and results for image generation, protein generation, depth estimation, pose prediction, and robotic manipulation.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds model-transfer experiments, MNIST generation analysis, Gaussian approximation-error measurements, and a constant score scaling comparison.

M1.justification: TSR's time-dependent score multiplier and its diffusion and flow implementations remain unchanged in Equations 6–9. The new parameter-selection guidance does not establish a revision to the sampling algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendices A.4–A.5 add unconditional MNIST digit generation and a four-component 2D Gaussian mixture for approximation testing. Existing datasets and the five application domains remain. Adding Flux extends model coverage within the existing text-to-image task.

E2.justification: Appendix A.6 and Figure 19 add constant score scaling to the checkerboard comparison and explicitly display unscaled DDPM alongside CNS and TSR; v1's Figure 3 showed data samples, CNS, and TSR. Existing comparator sets elsewhere are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols transfer fixed SD3 parameters (k=0.93, sigma=3) to SD2 and Flux, classify 1,000 MNIST samples per sampler, and measure relative score error while varying Gaussian separation and width at k=2. Figure 6 expands the protein parameter grid. These supplement retained protocols, including SD3's 5,000-image evaluation and 30 sampling steps.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands validation through quantitative MNIST mode-coverage analysis, score-error sensitivity to time and Gaussian geometry, and a CSS mode-collapse comparison in Appendices A.4–A.6. Table 1 additionally tests hyperparameter transfer across image models. Earlier image, pose, and depth ablations remain.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 first reports SD3 averages over five random seeds with accompanying plus/minus values; v1 gives point estimates without an SD3 run count. The uncertainty statistic is not identified. Robotic manipulation's three-seed reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds model-transfer scores, MNIST class frequencies, Gaussian error curves, CSS findings, and additional protein results. CNS generates MNIST digits 1 and 9 at 40.4% and 28.7%. SD3 baseline/TSR FID changes from 24.75/22.74 to five-seed summaries of 24.77/22.81; TSR CLIP changes from 33.07 to 33.05. Depth, pose, robotics, and the original SD2 appendix table retain their values.

T1.justification: Appendix A.6 newly defines CSS through its reverse-SDE formulation in Equation 10. The Gaussian derivations and Appendix B/C theorems and proofs otherwise remain substantively unchanged, apart from notation corrections. The expanded explanation and empirical error analysis do not add a proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same core contribution: training-free local temperature control through temporal score rescaling, compatibility with deterministic and stochastic samplers, and benefits across five application domains. Added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets parameter-transfer results as evidence of robustness across models and hypothesizes that shared stroke components explain CNS's MNIST digit bias. Section 5.3 expands the explanation of reduced depth variability. Existing limitations concerning local temperature scaling and restricted theoretical guarantees remain.

D1.justification: Section 5.6 adds practical alternating parameter-search guidance, and the new analyses disclose their settings. v2 removes the reproducibility paragraph explicitly promising supplementary Python implementation while retaining the project URL. This establishes removal of the disclosure, not withdrawal of the code itself.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for MNIST, Flux, and Skreta et al.'s Feynman–Kac correctors. Section 2 contrasts batch reweighting with TSR, and Appendix A.6 associates CSS with Skreta et al. The broader positioning against CFG, CNS, and training-based temperature sampling remains.

P1.justification: Analysis moves before Formulation, several explanatory paragraphs are expanded, and parameter-selection and impact sections are added while the reproducibility statement is removed. Most existing prose remains. New editorial problems include epsilon replacing k in Section 5.6 and an unresolved section reference in Appendix C.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column layout to a two-column conference format, extensively relocating and resizing displays. v2 adds Table 1 and Figures 16–19 and redraws Figure 6 with expanded axes and a reorganized legend. Most original figure imagery is retained.

improvement.justification: Relative to v1, quantitative mode-coverage testing, the CSS comparison, approximation-error diagnostics, parameter transfer, and five-seed SD3 reporting strengthen support for the unchanged method. These are useful extensions to an already broad empirical study. Undefined uncertainty notation, inconsistent tuning symbols, broken references, and removal of the explicit supplementary-code pointer limit the gain.
